Lately, I’ll see figures in the back seat of my cab, clear as anyone, but when I turn, no one’s there. Sometimes it’s my ex-wife, even though we’ve been divorced for years. I used to take pride in my work—keeping the car clean, knowing the city—but now, I don’t care. Finished fares, praise, doesn’t register. It’s like everything’s wrapped in cotton.  

People ask me questions, and I start talking about one thing, then it leads elsewhere. I lose the point, I know. My dispatcher yelled at me last week—said I didn’t answer his call, just went on about traffic patterns in a neighborhood I don’t even drive.  

I can’t tell if it’s the stress, the loneliness, or if my mind’s breaking. The sadness isn’t strong—it’s more like nothing matters, nothing touches me. And those visions? They don’t scare me. They just *are*.

I’ve been struggling for a while now—more than half a year, maybe close to a year. Lately, I’ll be at work in the ER and suddenly smell something burning, like flesh, but no one else does. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it feels so real. I’ve started worrying there’s something seriously wrong inside me—like my liver is rotting or my blood is poisoned. The doctors run tests, and everything comes back normal, but I can’t shake the feeling.  

Sleep’s been impossible. I wake up around 3 a.m. every night and just stay that way, pacing, pulling at my cuticles until they bleed. I used to love painting, going out with friends, even just watching movies, but now nothing feels like it matters. I cry a lot—sometimes for no reason—and other times, my thoughts just… jump. I’ll be talking to a patient about their chest pain and suddenly say something about my shoes or the weather, and I don’t know how I got there.  

It’s hard to focus at work. I’m making little mistakes, forgetting meds. I still show up, but I’m not the nurse I used to be. The sadness and the weird thoughts have both been going on for so long, overlapping in a way I can’t untangle.

Lately, though, I can’t stop crying at work—little things set me off, and I’ve lost interest in everything, even things I used to love, like painting and seeing my friends. I haven’t been sleeping right either—I wake up two or three times every night and can’t go back to sleep, just lying there, restless, pacing my room, picking at my skin until it bleeds.  

For the past six months, I’ve also been convinced something’s poisoning my blood—like my organs are rotting. I smell this awful metallic stench, like burnt hair or chemicals, but no one else does. I told the doctor last month, and she checked my labs—everything was normal. I’ve been jumping from one thought to the next during handoffs at work—my speech gets all tangled, and I can see the confusion on my colleagues’ faces.  

The mood stuff has been there almost the whole time, really. But there were two weeks last fall, after a panic attack at work, when I wasn’t as depressed, but I still smelled the odor and believed my blood was toxic. That’s when they sent me here.

I think she’s been sending me signs—small things, like a song on the radio or the way the sparks fly.

As a news anchor, I’m used to being sharp, on top of things, but I started feeling… off. I’d be on air and swear the teleprompter messages had hidden meanings just for me—like they were sending me signals only I could understand. Even random comments from coworkers felt like secret messages directed at me.  

Then, I began feeling this crawling sensation on my skin, like bugs moving underneath, but no one else could see anything. It still happens. My thoughts? They jump around—today I’ll be talking about a script, then suddenly I’m thinking about guilt, how I must’ve caused that plane crash last winter, even though I wasn’t even near it. I know that sounds irrational, but the guilt feels real, crushing.  

I’ve lost all interest in things I used to love—makeup, fashion, even anchoring. I feel empty. I’ve gained over twenty pounds recently, just from not caring. And honestly, this low mood? It’s been here most of the time, longer than the breaks between my strange thoughts and sensations. In fact, there were only a few weeks last spring when I wasn’t depressed, but the delusions and hallucinations still crept in.
D007-D005_h008.question_b:
I’ve been feeling completely disconnected for over a year now. At first, I noticed things on the news—certain phrases, even the way anchors looked into the camera—that I just *knew* were coded messages meant for me. People on the street would glance my way, and I could feel their words crawling on my skin, like insects, though nothing was there. I still feel that—like something’s moving under my clothes or brushing my arms when no one’s near.

My thoughts? They jump around so much. I’ll start talking about the broadcast schedule, then remember my mother’s birthday, then think about how the government’s tracking me through the teleprompter—things that don’t connect, I know, but in the moment, they feel linked.

The past year has been heavy, but honestly, I don’t even feel sad—I feel empty. I stopped cooking, painting, everything. I gained weight, I don’t know how. I once believed I’d caused a car accident just by thinking negatively that morning, even though I wasn’t anywhere near it. But here’s the thing—the low mood, the guilt, the emptiness—they weren’t there *all* the time. The paranoia and the sensations, those never really stopped. The depression came in waves, but the rest? That’s been constant.

D007-D005_h025.question_both:
I’ve been feeling… disconnected. For the past year or so—maybe a little longer—things just don’t feel real. At first, it was small: the taste of metal in my mouth even when I wasn’t eating anything. I’d brush my teeth and still taste blood. Now, sometimes I sit in my classroom and forget why I’m there. I’ll start answering a student’s question and end up talking about something else entirely—like the sky cracking open. That’s how I know it’s happening. I can’t stop thinking about the end of everything. Not in a dramatic way—more like… it’s already over, and we just don’t realize it yet.

Sleep’s worse. Night after night, I dream the world collapses slowly. Not fire or war—just silence. Everyone stops moving. I wake up panicked, heart racing, pacing my room. Can’t sit. Can’t stay still. But during the day? Some afternoons, I just freeze at my desk. Students have to call my name three times. I don’t feel sad—just… numb. Like I used to love music, movies, even grading a good essay. Now, nothing. I don’t even care. I don’t know how much of this is depression and how much is something else. Time blurs. Some days feel like weeks. I can’t tell what’s what anymore.
D007-D005_h025.question_a:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half or more—just trying to get through the day. As a teacher, I used to love engaging with my students, but now I can’t seem to feel anything. It’s like I’m numb inside, even during moments that should bring joy. I don’t sleep well—night after night, I wake up drenched in sweat from these awful dreams, like the school is collapsing or my students are vanishing into nothing.  

About a year and a half ago, things really started unraveling. I became convinced the world was ending—like, truly ending—and that nothing matters because it’ll all be wiped out soon. Sometimes, I’ll taste something metallic, even when I haven’t eaten anything. I don’t know where it comes from. My mind wanders when people talk to me; I answer questions but go off on tangents because the connections feel so urgent, even if others don’t see them. There were days I just sat at home, couldn’t move, couldn’t respond—just frozen.  

Even when I’m not feeling this crushing dread, the delusions and strange tastes linger. But honestly, the depression has been there longer than not—it’s been with me through most of this whole ordeal.
D007-D005_h025.question_b:
I’ve been a high school teacher for over ten years, and honestly, I can’t remember the last time I felt like myself. Lately, everything feels… off. For the past year and a half, I’ve been convinced the world is ending—like, literally crumbling. Not in a metaphorical way. I taste metal all the time, even when I’m not eating anything. It’s like someone poisoned the air. I’ve tried explaining this to my principal, but I went off on some tangent about government signals in the water, and he just stared at me. I didn’t even answer his question about grading.

There are days I just sit in my classroom after school, frozen. No energy to move. My students say hi, and I don’t respond. Not because I don’t care—because it all feels pointless. Nothing matters. I used to love coaching debate, but now even that feels empty. I haven’t gone out with friends in forever. Honestly, nothing brings joy anymore.

I’ve been having nightmares too—vivid ones—about floods swallowing the school. I pace my apartment all night, rubbing my hands raw. But these low moods? They come and go. The paranoia, the voices, the taste of rust—that’s what’s constant. The sadness is just… there sometimes.
